papers.title: Can Active Learning Experience Be Transferred?
papers.abstract: Active learning is an important machine learning problem in reducing the human labeling effort. Current active learning strategies are designed from human knowledge, and are applied on each dataset in an immutable manner. In other words, experience about the usefulness of strategies cannot be updated and transferred to improve active learning on other datasets. This paper initiates a pioneering study on whether active learning experience can be transferred. We first propose a novel active learning model that linearly aggregates existing strategies. The linear weights can then be used to represent the active learning experience. We equip the model with the popular linear upper- confidence-bound (LinUCB) algorithm for contextual bandit to update the weights. Finally, we extend our model to transfer the experience across datasets with the technique of biased regularization. Empirical studies demonstrate that the learned experience not only is competitive with existing strategies on most single datasets, but also can be transferred across datasets to improve the performance on future learning tasks.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究主动学习中的经验迁移，与FEA替代模型、昂贵仿真采样或植入物设计问题无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on active learning for classification tasks, with no connection to surrogate modeling for expensive simulations, uncertainty quantification, constraints handling, or biomechanics/implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索主动学习经验能否跨数据集迁移。
summary_zh.method: 提出线性聚合策略，结合LinUCB算法更新权重，使用偏置正则化实现迁移。
summary_zh.result: 迁移后的经验能提升未来学习任务的性能。
summary_zh.validation: 在多个标准数据集上通过实验比较验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate whether active learning experience can be transferred across different datasets.
summary_en.method: Proposes a linear aggregation model of existing strategies updated with LinUCB and biased regularization for transfer.
summary_en.result: Learned experience improves performance on future learning tasks after transfer.
summary_en.validation: Empirical evaluation on multiple benchmark datasets compared to baseline strategies.

papers.title: Manufacturing of Ti–6Al–4V Micro‐Implantable Parts Using Hybrid Selective Laser Melting and Micro‐Electrical Discharge Machining
papers.abstract: This research is carried out to cover the gap in producing high-precision micro-components using SLM as well as to study the potential of using µ-EDM in the field of additive manufacturing. The process offers an optimized technique to manufacture high-quality micro implantable components with the highest density and the best surface finish.
papers.first_author_affiliation: School of Mechanical and Automotive Engineering Kingston University London SW15 3DW United Kingdom

corresponding_authors.name: Hany Hassanin
corresponding_authors.affiliation: School of Mechanical and Automotive Engineering Kingston University London SW15 3DW United Kingdom

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文涉及Ti-6Al-4V微植入体的制造工艺，但未关注应力屏蔽、疲劳或骨整合等力学与生物学性能。
llm.why_not_core: Does not address stress shielding, fatigue, or osseointegration; focuses on manufacturing precision rather than mechanical or biological performance.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高SLM微零件精度和表面质量
summary_zh.method: 混合使用SLM与微电火花加工
summary_zh.result: 获得高密度、高表面光洁度的微植入件
summary_zh.validation: 实验测量密度和表面粗糙度

summary_en.motivation: To bridge the gap in producing high-precision micro-components via SLM by integrating micro-EDM for improved surface finish and density.
summary_en.method: A hybrid process combining selective laser melting with micro-electrical discharge machining is developed.
summary_en.result: Micro-implantable Ti-6Al-4V parts with high density and superior surface finish are achieved.
summary_en.validation: Experimental characterization of density and surface roughness validates the process improvements.

papers.title: Conferring biological activity to native spider silk: A biofunctionalized protein‐based microfiber
papers.abstract: Spider silk is an extraordinary material with physical properties comparable to the best scaffolding/structural materials, and as a fiber it can be manipulated with ease into a variety of configurations. Our work here demonstrates that natural spider silk fibers can also be used to organize biological components on and in devices through rapid and simple means. Micron scale spider silk fibers (5-10 μm in diameter) were surface modified with a variety of biological entities engineered with pentaglutamine tags via microbial transglutaminase (mTG). Enzymes, enzyme pathways, antibodies, and fluorescent proteins were all assembled onto spider silk fibers using this biomolecular engineering/biofabrication process. Additionally, arrangement of biofunctionalized fiber should in of itself generate a secondary level of biomolecular organization. Toward this end, as proofs of principle, spatially defined arrangement of biofunctionalized spider silk fiber was shown to generate effects specific to silk position in two cases. In one instance, arrangement perpendicular to a flow produced selective head and neck carcinoma cell capture on silk with antibodies complexed to conjugated protein G. In a second scenario, asymmetric bacterial chemotaxis arose from asymmetric conjugation of enzymes to arranged silk. Overall, the biofabrication processes used here were rapid, required no complex chemistries, were biologically benign, and also the resulting engineered silk microfibers were flexible, readily manipulated and functionally active. Deployed here in microfluidic environments, biofunctional spider silk fiber provides a means to convey complex biological functions over a range of scales, further extending its potential as a biomaterial in biotechnological settings. Biotechnol. Bioeng. 2017;114: 83-95. © 2016 Wiley Periodicals, Inc.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及蜘蛛丝的生物功能化，与AI生物打印方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: No AI or machine learning used; purely experimental biofunctionalization without computational modeling or autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种快速、简单的方法赋予蜘蛛丝生物活性。
summary_zh.method: 利用微生物转谷氨酰胺酶将带有五谷氨酰胺标签的生物分子固定在蜘蛛丝纤维表面。
summary_zh.result: 成功组装了酶、抗体、荧光蛋白等，并展示了空间排列产生的生物学效应。
summary_zh.validation: 通过细胞捕获和细菌趋化实验验证功能。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a rapid and simple method to confer biological activity to native spider silk fibers.
summary_en.method: Surface modification of micron-scale spider silk fibers with biological entities via microbial transglutaminase and pentaglutamine tags.
summary_en.result: Successful assembly of enzymes, antibodies, and fluorescent proteins on silk, with spatial organization yielding cell capture and chemotaxis effects.
summary_en.validation: Functional validation through selective carcinoma cell capture and asymmetric bacterial chemotaxis in microfluidic devices.
